The first and third columns are equal. cbind(res1$lambda[1:5], res1$lambda_component[1:5], mu1 + res1$lambda_component[1:5]) #>          [,1]     [,2]     [,3] #> [1,] 0.900000 0.600000 0.900000 #> [2,] 0.438383 0.138383 0.438383 #> [3,] 1.431282 1.131282 1.431282 #> [4,] 2.027111 1.727111 2.027111 #> [5,] 2.335269 2.035269 2.335269 # The second and third columns are equal except in the initial row. cbind(res1$lambda[1:5], res1$rambda[1:5], res1$lambda[1:5] + alpha1) #>          [,1]     [,2]     [,3] #> [1,] 0.900000 0.900000 2.100000 #> [2,] 0.438383 1.638383 1.638383 #> [3,] 1.431282 2.631282 2.631282 #> [4,] 2.027111 3.227111 3.227111 #> [5,] 2.335269 3.535269 3.535269 # By definition, the following two are equal: res1$lambda[2:6] #> [1] 0.438383 1.431282 2.027111 2.335269 3.011391 mu1 + (res1$rambda[1:5] - mu1) * exp(-beta1 * res1$inter_arrival[2:6]) #> [1] 0.438383 1.431282 2.027111 2.335269 3.011391 logLik(hspec1, inter_arrival = res1$inter_arrival) #> The initial values for intensity processes are not provided. Internally determined initial values are used. #> loglikelihood  #>     -214.2385 # Initial parameter values for numerical optimization. mu0 <- 0.5; alpha0 <- 1.0; beta0 <- 1.8 hspec0 <- new("hspec", mu = mu0, alpha = alpha0, beta = beta0) #
